newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chips edge lower as investors digest gains.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips edge lower as investors digest gains.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks slipped Monday as investors regrouped after the market set records in six straight sessions.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 4.07 points at 7,777.97 after Friday's record finish of 7,782.04.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 12-10 on volume of 236 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The technology-laden Nasdaq composite index rose 3.53 points to 1426.56 as several key tech stocks posted strong gains.

"I think you are seeing a little bit of a reversal from last week," when the technology sector was flagging and blue chips steamed higher, said Gail Dudack, chief investment strategist at UBS Securities.

Tom Carpenter, a managing director and chief economist at ASB Capital Management Inc., said this level of strength in the economy and the stock market occurs once every 100 years so it is of little concern if the Dow is pausing for a day.
"Stocks have had a terrific run and the longer term picture here is optimistic," he said.

He said that several factors have fuelled the market's recent rally, including a possible cut in the capital gains tax and economic data that suggest the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates.
"All these things are positive and on top of that we have a very suportive bond market," Carpenter said.
The only possible threat to the market's short term outlook is a "maverick statistic" which could trigger a slide.
"When the stock market has been fed such incredible fundamental data, the market is vulnerable to some statistical setbacks or announcement setbacks," Carpenter said.

Arun Kumar, equities strategist at Lehman Brothers, said the market was awaiting the May Consumer Price Index report due on Tuesday. Economists are forecasting a 0.2 percent rise. Last week, the government reported that producer prices fell for the fifth straight month in May, dropping by 0.3 percent.
It was the first time in 45 years that wholesale prices have dropped for five consecutive months.

Among the technology issues, Intel Corp. gained 1-7/8 to 146-5/8. The chip maker plans to unveil new machines called NetPCs in conjunction with Microsoft and several computer makers that would lower the cost of computer networks.
Dell Computer climbed 3-1/8 to 114-1/4, Compaq Computer rose 3-3/8 to 103-3/4 and Applied Materials Inc. gained 7/8 to 65-1/4.
Elsewhere, DuPont Co. climbed one to 59-7/8.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks edged up 0.10 of a point to 893.37. The American Stock Exchange index fell 2.14 points to 627.96.
